newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Great Eagle spinoff decision welcomed.
newsitem.headline: Great Eagle spinoff decision welcomed.

text.p: Investors gave the thumbs up on Monday to the decision by Great Eagle Holdings Ltd to shelve its spinoff of Tai Shan Properties Ltd.
Shares in Great Eagle Holdings jumped HK$1.85 to HK$30.90 on turnover of 4.6 million after the company aborted the spinoff of its office and commercial property portfolio.
Great Eagle said lowering the issue price would have resulted in an unacceptable level of dilution to Great Eagle.
Pamela Lam, an analyst at Pacific Challenge Securities, said: "There is no point spinning off the unit when market sentiment is not in favour of the issue."
Analysts did not think that Great Eagle would be hurt by the decision to scupper the spinoff.
"What does it mean for Great Eagle? Probably not a great deal," said Michael Leary of Lehman Brothers, adding that the decision made Great Eagle more of a buy.
"It's a very attractive (buying) opportunity in share price terms," Leary said.
Great Eagle's share price has fallen from HK$36.20 on January 20 to HK$29.05 on February 28 ahead of the flotation.
"In the short run, it will have a positive impact on the share price," said Tai Fook Securities' Edmond Yuen.
Trading at a 40 percent discount to net asset value (NAV), against an average 30 percent for property companies indicated there was room for Great Eagle shares to rise, he said.
The issue was intended to finance its redevelopment project in Hong Kong's Mong Kok district with the Land Development Corp.

In January, Edward Lui of Nikko Research Center, estimated Great Eagle had already committed about HK$2.9 billion to the Mong Kok project up to December 1996, and net debt of HK$6.3 billion at September 30 last year.
Despite the issue's cancellation -- and projected oversupply in the Grade A office sector, a core part of Tai Shan Property -- Leary was bullish on Great Eagle.
Leary said Great Eagle had renegotiated a good portion of its leases, locking in rentals till about the year 2000.
"It's a long way to go between now and then," Leary said.
Great Eagle's hotel strategy was paying off - 1997 would be a good year, followed by an even better one in 1998, Leary said.
Great Eagle owns the four-star Eaton Hotel and the five-star Hong Kong Renaissance Hotel in Tsim Sha Tsui tourist district, and has interests in three hotels outside Hong Kong.
Meanwhile, analysts said Great Eagle could pursue alternative sources of cash, including a share issue.
"You can't rule out the possibility that it will have a share placement in Great Eagle later on," Nikko's Lui said.
Lui said Hysan Development Co Ltd and Cheung Kong (Holdings) Ltd had raised funds relatively cheaply through the loan market.
Leary said Great Eagle could raise 50 percent to 60 percent of the money it needed through bank financing.
Lam said Great Eagle's need for funding in Mong Kok was fuelling speculation that it might consider a placement, a syndicated loan or even a bond issue.
But Yuen said the interest costs of bank financing could increase the company's financial burden - and its debt ratio.

According to BasisField, an Asian debt markets database, Great Eagle's major foray into the loan market was in 1995, when it was one of five guarantors for the US$512.31 million refinancing of Citibank Plaza in Hong Kong's Central district.
Great Eagle owns 69.5 percent of Citibank Plaza.
